question: is there a cheap pre-graft crossmatch: does host W_out row-norm mean at graft sites (P1, e059's interface signal) or pre-graft stream-cosine (P2) predict graft damage D across host x donor pairs, partial on A?

registered_design.D: mean over graft sites {2,3} of dCE(host<-donor mlp-Lsite), 15 fixed e052 batches (e059-verbatim)
registered_design.A: host own-organ ablation dCE, same sites/batches (e063 method)
registered_design.P1: host W_out row-norm mean at graft sites (e059 axis)
registered_design.P2: mean token-cosine of host/donor residual streams on shared 2-batch probe, per depth; graft-input aggregate = d2,d3
registered_design.bars: winner: |partial r(D|A)| >= 0.5 AND host-cluster bootstrap 95% CI excludes 0 AND n_pairs >= 20
registered_design.outcome_if_neither: cheap predictor dead; P2 program pivots to trained tolerance

scale_A.hosts_note: 12-net pool full square + 6 e050 directed-mutation nets as hosts only

label_definition.rule: D > median(D) over all scale-A pairs

P1.label: P1: host W_out row-norm mean (graft sites)

donor_win.label: secondary: donor W_in row-norm mean (graft sites)

scale_B_secondary.note: 2.7M cohort, n=6 directional pairs — no bars claimed

verdict: P2 WINS the cheap crossmatch: pre-graft stream-cosine (graft-input depths) partial r(D|A) -0.976 (host-cluster CI [-0.983842131896601, -0.962811064838978]) over 204 pairs; decision rule: graft only if cos_graftinput >= 0.4459 (AUC 0.919, Youden J 0.657)
